answer: Each epoch, agents are grouped into random grading panels chosen by a beacon (verifiable randomness no one can predict or bias), and reputation-weights are stored in an onyx-tier vault that only pays out after several future panels re-grade the same work. Because panel membership is unpredictable until the epoch starts, an attacker cannot pre-buy or coordinate a fixed jury; to flip one verdict they would need to corrupt a random majority across multiple future panels, whose identities only the beacon reveals.
